metaDescription: Six Frigidaire countertop ice makers compared: bullet and square-cube models at 26 lb and nugget machines at 33 and 44 lb, with size, speed and upkeep notes.
expertTake: The Frigidaire Gallery 44 lb nugget maker is the top pick for a home that wants chewable ice from a brand with a service network. The Frigidaire EFIC189 square-cube unit is the pick for slow-melting cubes at a modest price. Skip the 26 lb bullet models if you drink a lot of iced beverages, because a basket that holds about 2 pounds empties in a couple of rounds.
introParagraphs: One major appliance brand's countertop range covers three different mechanisms under one name. A bullet unit freezes ice on chilled prongs, a square-cube unit freezes water in a tray, and a nugget unit scrapes a frozen cylinder with an auger. They look similar on a counter and behave very differently in use.

Brand familiarity matters most for after-sale support, parts and the confidence that a manual and a service line exist. Within the brand we compare the machines on ice type, output, speed, size and the cleaning they need, then rank who each one suits.

products.name: Frigidaire Gallery countertop nugget ice maker, 44 lb, cream, touch panel
products.description:
The Gallery's nugget design scrapes ice from a cold cylinder with an auger and presses it into soft, crunchy pellets, and at 44 pounds a day it is the highest-output Frigidaire countertop machine. Touch buttons control it, and a drawer with a viewing window shows how full the bin is without opening anything.

Frigidaire calls it compact enough to fit under cabinets, which matters because nugget machines are tall. Auto self-cleaning handles routine flushing, though scale on the cylinder still needs a periodic descale. The cream finish is a styling choice that stands out in a kitchen.

Against the 33 lb nugget models it makes a third more ice. Place it with vent clearance, descale every month or two and keep an eye on the bin through the window.
products.bestFor: Homes that want a high-output chewable-ice machine from a major brand.
pros: 44 lb per day is the top Frigidaire countertop output
Drawer and viewing window show ice level
cons: Nugget machines are louder than bullet units
Cream finish may not suit every kitchen

products.name: Frigidaire touchscreen nugget ice maker, 33 lb, slate, 20 min self-clean
products.description:
A touchscreen replaces the buttons on this Frigidaire, and the headline convenience is an automatic cleaning cycle that completes in about 20 minutes. For a machine that most owners neglect, a short cycle is a real reason it will actually get run.

Daily output reaches 33 pounds of light, crunchy nugget ice that blends into drinks and absorbs their flavor. The slate finish suits modern kitchens. Like every nugget machine it is heavier and louder than a bullet unit, and the cleaning cycle flushes but does not descale.

Compared with the Gallery 44 lb it makes less and adds a screen and a faster clean. Descale on schedule, keep vent clearance and let the machine dry if it will sit idle.
products.bestFor: Owners who want an easy, quick self-cleaning cycle.
pros: Automatic cleaning cycle in about 20 minutes
cons: Output is a third lower than the 44 lb Gallery
Cleaning cycle does not remove scale

products.name: Frigidaire EFIC228 countertop nugget ice maker, 33 lb, compact, metallic
products.description:
The EFIC228 is the straightforward nugget machine in the range: 33 pounds a day, soft crunchy ice and a compact countertop body in a metallic finish. The maker claims you will be enjoying ice within about 15 minutes, a slower start than newer nugget makers but a fair figure for a first batch.

It plugs into any outlet and is light enough to take to a campsite. The trade-off is feature count: there is no touchscreen and no fast cleaning cycle, so it is simpler and cheaper. Nugget ice here is the same as in the pricier models.

Compared with the touchscreen model it is plainer and slower to start. Descale regularly, keep vents clear and wipe the bin every couple of weeks.
products.bestFor: Shoppers who want Frigidaire nugget ice at the lowest price.
cons: 15 minute start is slower than newer models
No touchscreen or fast clean cycle

products.name: Frigidaire EFIC189 compact ice maker, 26 lb, two cube sizes, silver
products.description:
This model makes square, clear cubes instead of bullets, in under six minutes per batch, with a choice of two cube sizes. The reservoir sits beneath the ice basket, a layout that keeps the footprint small, and the basket stores up to about 2.2 pounds before the machine pauses.

Square cubes melt slower than bullets and look better in a glass, a plus for cocktails and display. Output is 26 pounds a day, the same as the bullet models. Nothing here is automated beyond the basics, so it is a simple, durable machine.

Compared with the black bullet model it adds a cube-shape and size choice at the same output. Clean the reservoir regularly, descale every month or two and let the machine dry if it will be idle.
products.bestFor: Cocktail and drink fans who want slow-melting square cubes.
pros: Square clear cubes melt slower than bullets

products.name: Frigidaire 26 lb portable bullet ice maker, black stainless steel
products.description:
This is the machine most people picture when they think of a Frigidaire countertop ice maker: a compact portable unit that makes nine bullet cubes about every seven minutes, up to 26 pounds a day, in a black stainless steel body. A transparent window lets you see the ice level and the batch forming.

Bullet ice is hard and quick to make, with a pointed shape that packs a cooler well. The seven minute cycle is slower than the six-minute claims of some newer machines, and the basket stops the machine when it fills. As with all bullet makers, melted ice drains back to the reservoir, so stored ice shrinks.

Compared with the EFIC189 it makes bullets instead of squares. Keep the vents clear, descale monthly and dry the machine if it will sit.
products.bestFor: Everyday ice with a familiar brand and a simple interface.
pros: Nine bullet cubes about every seven minutes
cons: Stored ice melts back into the reservoir
7 minute cycle is not the fastest

products.name: Frigidaire EFIC128 compact countertop ice maker, 26 lb, black, large window

specList.label: Design
specList.value: Modern with a large transparent window

products.description:
The EFIC128 is the compact, modern take on the bullet maker, with a large transparent window so you can watch ice form and see the level. Daily output is 26 pounds, the same as as the other Frigidaire bullet models, in a small black body.

Frigidaire pitches it for a wide range of uses because of its small size, from a kitchen counter to a camper. The window is the main usability feature, as a full basket pauses production and you can see it. Like all bullet makers it is quick, cheap and loses stored ice to melting.

Compared with the black stainless bullet model it is smaller with a bigger window. Check the dimensions against your space, descale regularly and keep vent clearance.
products.bestFor: Small counters and campers that want a simple compact unit.
cons: Stored ice melts back into the reservoir
Output is modest for a busy household

buyingCriteria.explanation: Frigidaire's countertop range spans three ice types. Bullet makers like the EFIC128 and the black stainless unit freeze hard cubes quickly. The EFIC189 freezes square cubes that melt slower. The Gallery and EFIC228 nugget models make soft chewable pellets with an auger. Decide the ice first, since none can switch.

Daily output runs from 26 pounds on the bullet and cube models to 33 and 44 on the nugget models. The EFIC189 stores about 2.2 pounds in its basket, and the others hold a similar amount before pausing. For a busy household, a pause is the limiting factor, not the daily rating.

The Gallery and touchscreen nugget models have automatic cleaning cycles, with the touchscreen model finishing in about 20 minutes. None of the machines removes mineral scale automatically. A monthly or bimonthly descale with citric acid is the real maintenance.

Nugget machines run an auger and a compressor, so they are louder than bullet and cube makers. Place the machine on a solid counter with several inches of clearance, away from a bedroom wall. A cabinet that traps heat raises noise and cuts output. If you plan to run a nugget machine under a cabinet, leave an open front and a gap at the back so the compressor can exhale, and test it for a day before you decide the spot works.

Nugget machines are taller than bullet makers, and Frigidaire says the Gallery fits under cabinets. Bullet units like the EFIC128 are compact enough for a small counter or a camper. Measure your space and check the dimensions against the listing before ordering. Allow for the clearance the maker specifies around the vents, usually several inches, as well as the height needed to lift a lid or pull out a drawer.

A major appliance brand means a manual, a service line and parts that are easier to find than from a no-name seller. That matters most in year three, when a pump or a sensor fails. Weigh the extra cost of a known brand against how much you depend on the machine. Check the warranty length and the claim process before you buy, and keep your receipt, since a countertop appliance is cheap enough that many owners skip registration and regret it later.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ice type fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We ranked each machine within its own ice type. The Gallery led nugget machines, the EFIC189 led cubes and the black stainless model led bullets. We did not compare across types.

howWeEvaluated.title: Output and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at daily output from 26 to 44 pounds and the basket capacity of about 2.2 pounds on the EFIC189. A pause when the basket fills limits party use. Output claims were treated as best-case.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning features
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the Gallery's auto cleaning and the touchscreen model's 20 minute cycle with the plainer models. Faster cleaning scored higher. None removes scale, which we noted for all.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and size
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered auger noise, body height and fit under cabinets. Bullet units scored for quiet and compactness. Nugget models scored for ice quality.

howWeEvaluated.title: Support
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited the Frigidaire brand for manuals and service. We noted that a major brand does not replace regular descaling. Simpler models scored for fewer parts to fail.

cards.label: Nugget
cards.text: The Gallery, touchscreen and EFIC228 make soft chewable pellets. They are taller, louder and pricier.

cards.label: Bullet and cube
cards.text: The EFIC128, black stainless and EFIC189 make hard cubes quickly. They are lighter, quieter and cheaper.

howToChoose.note: Nugget for chewing and flavor; bullet or cube for speed and price.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A compact body, a window to check the ice level and a design that fits under cabinets.

cards.text: The EFIC128 is the smallest. The Gallery claims it fits under cabinets despite being a nugget machine.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want chewable ice daily or a quick clean routine. The Gallery and touchscreen models repay.

cards.text: You want plain cubes occasionally. The EFIC128 or the black stainless model is enough.

maintenance.why: Scale cuts output and clouds the ice. Run a citric acid cycle or Frigidaire's recommended cleaner through the reservoir to clear it.
It flushes the reservoir of residue. It slows biofilm but does not replace descaling, and on the plainer models it is the only built-in help you get, so schedule it rather than waiting for a smell.

A damp bin grows film, and a cloudy window hides the ice level. A soft cloth with a drop of mild cleaner and a rinse is enough, and avoid abrasive pads that scratch the window and leave rough spots where scale gathers.

When dust clogs the rear vents of a Frigidaire countertop unit, the compressor runs hotter and daily output drops. A soft brush on the grille and a few inches of space on every side keep the compressor cool and quiet, and cost nothing to maintain.
Standing water grows slime. Drain the reservoir, wipe it dry and leave the lid open, so the next time you power up after a long gap the machine starts clean and does not need an extra flush.

faq.q: Which Frigidaire countertop ice maker makes the most ice?
faq.a: The Gallery nugget model claims 44 pounds a day. The touchscreen and EFIC228 nugget models claim 33, and the bullet and cube models claim 26. Real output is lower in a warm room. In a hot kitchen with warm tap water, a 26 pound machine may deliver closer to twenty, so size your expectation to your conditions and not to the label.

faq.q: Is nugget ice worth the extra cost?
faq.a: If you like chewable ice that absorbs flavor, yes. Nugget machines cost more, run louder and weigh more than bullet makers. They also need more attention to scale, because the auger and cylinder are the heart of the machine, so budget a little time each month for descaling.

faq.q: Does the self-cleaning cycle remove scale?
faq.a: No. It flushes the reservoir but not mineral buildup. Descale with citric acid or a maker-approved cleaner every month or two. After descaling, run a couple of clean-water cycles and discard the first ice, since leftover descaler gives the ice an off taste that is easy to mistake for a bad machine.

faq.q: How much ice does the basket hold?
faq.a: About 2.2 pounds on the EFIC189, and a similar amount on the others. When it is full the machine stops, so bag the ice if you need more. For a gathering, empty the basket into a freezer bag every hour, which keeps the machine producing and keeps the ice from melting back into the reservoir.

faq.q: Do these machines keep ice frozen?
faq.a: No. Stored ice slowly melts into the reservoir below, so the pile in the basket shrinks if left alone. Use it fresh or bag and freeze it. The machine is a producer, not a storage unit, so think of it as a faucet for ice that you fill into something else rather than a freezer on the counter.

faq.q: Can I use these in an RV?
faq.a: Yes, they plug into a standard outlet and are portable. Let a moved machine stand upright for a few hours before powering on. A camper counter is often small and warm, so check the clearance and keep the machine out of direct sun, because heat is what slows a compressor most.
